{"body":"**Summary**

Reactivity today is fine-grained: a node re-emits `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY` when a signal bound to its text/property changes (`node.textBinding` / `node.propertyBindings`), and structural slots (`NavigationContainer`, `Conditional`) re-render via `Emitter.reconcileSlot` when their selector signal changes. That covers signals that a node *binds to* — but not signals a view *reads* to decide its structure.

**The gap**

A view that reads a signal inside `render()`/`body()` to pick its subtree (control flow: which branch to render, which router, which destination) is not reactive. `body()` is evaluated once at mount and never re-runs, so that read's dependency is never recorded and no structural change is ever emitted.

**Scope: ALL signals, any source**

This applies to every signal, no matter where it comes from:

- environment values (`Environment.value(key)` returns a `Signal<T>`; a bound node updates, but a `body()` read for control flow does not);
- `State` / `StateStore` signals and `PersistentState` values;
- a `Signals.signal` / `Signals.computed` captured directly by the view;
- host-provided signals (`Platform.ACTIVE_PATH`, viewport, theme, etc.).

Any node whose render depends on a signal should emit its structural changes when that signal changes.

**Mechanism (suggested)**

Generalize `Emitter.reconcileSlot`: render a subtree as a *tracked* computation so that when any signal it read during `render()`/`body()` changes, the subtree re-renders and the structural deltas are emitted.

**Constraints (non-negotiable)**

- Preserve fine-grained per-node reactivity elsewhere — an unchanged node still emits **zero** opcodes.
- Renderers stay stateless (Principle 1).
- Steady-state emission stays allocation-free.
- The diff-based emitter contract is unchanged: only actual changes are transmitted.

**Related**

- `Environment.value(key)` returns signals (feat/environment-signals).
- `spec/DSL.md` §4.5, `AGENTS.md` reactive-signals section, `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`.

  signals (`source`/`playing`/`position`/`volume`/`muted`/`loop`/`rate`, each
  rebindable to an app-owned `WritableSignal` so the controller drives the state

  convenience transport
  (`play`/`pause`/`toggle`/`seek`/`setVolume`/`setMuted`/`setLoop`/`setRate`).
  A report never writes a command signal (spec/MEDIA.md §4.2): e.g. a
  `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` (the natural-end stop, or a media error) feeds
  `playingReport`, so the app's `PLAYBACK_STATE` intent survives and the track
  advanced on `MEDIA_ENDED` keeps playing.
  The emitter materializes **one `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node per controller** (in
  place at its `attach()` marker, with a **pinned** id). The pinned id is
  reserved in the id allocator (no other node can take it) and honored on **every**
  emission path — including a subtree re-emission that reassigns ids (`freshIdFor`)

  tears down playback. A controller must therefore be created **once** by the app

  `InputDispatcher`; the report feeds are separate from the command binding, so a

State<Integer> total = new State<>(0, "total");   // explicit store key

```

The store (`StateStore`) is untyped and platform-neutral (in-memory, Redis,
file, SQLite, LocalStorage, NVS flash). The Java realization wires `State`
fields via an annotation processor that generates a `<View>_StateBinder` per
view class; connection happens when the view renders. A generated DSL in a
language without reflection/annotation processing MUST offer the equivalent
explicit wiring.

### 3.4 Structural reactivity (conditional rendering)

The tree is normally static once mounted (["`body()` is evaluated once at
mount"](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)); the **only** sanctioned way to
change *structure* reactively is a **structural container**: a slot whose
single child subtree is selected by a signal and **reconciled** when the
signal changes. This is the foundation for `if`/`else`, `switch`, and
navigation ([§4.5](#45-navigation)).

| Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL | Rust DSL | Emits |
|----------------------------|----------|----------|-------|
| `if cond { then } else { else }` in a result builder | `Conditional.when(Signal<Boolean>, View then, View else)` | plain `if`/`match` in `build()` | `TREE` deltas (reconcile) |
| `switch value { case a -> v; default -> d }` | `Conditional.when(Signal<T>, Case.of(T, View)...)` + `Case.otherwise(View)` | plain `if`/`match` in `build()` | `TREE` deltas (reconcile) |

**Java realization** (`com.pathland.view.Conditional`): statically importable
lowercase factories on a final class with a private constructor, mirroring
[`Signals`](#31-signal-surface):

```java
import static com.pathland.view.Conditional.when;
import static com.pathland.view.Conditional.Case;

Current sanctioned model:
- Fine-grained bindings for text/property.
- Structural reactivity only via explicit structural containers: Conditional.when, NavigationContainer, SizeThatFits.

#88 asks to automatically track ANY signal read during render/body and re-render that subtree, generalizing reconcileSlot.

Benefits:
1. Ergonomic: ordinary `if (signal.get())` / `switch` in body becomes reactive without manual Conditional wrapper. Removes boilerplate and the "silent staleness" footgun where a read in body looks reactive but isn't.

# pathland-view (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 27, 2026

The hand-written, framework-agnostic Java 17+ DSL (`dev.pathland.view`):
declarative views, Angular-style signals, fine-grained emitter, `PLPL` wire
codec, lazy JNA ring interop, and cross-platform `State`. Protocol contract:
`spec/`. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.

## Implemented

- **`ProxyView`** (`ProxyView.make(p -> p.endpoint(...).route(...).credential(...))`):
  a `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) container whose child subtree is served by **another**
  Pathland server (spec/PROXY.md). It authors **no** children — the origin root is
  spliced in at runtime — and takes size modifiers like any view. The immutable
  `ProxyConfig` snapshot rides the node (`PathlandNode.proxyConfig`) and is
  surfaced to the host through `RenderResult.proxyViews()` (node id → config) so
  `pathland-server-core` opens an origin connection per proxy node. The emitter's
  internal `onStructureReconciled(Runnable)` hook (like `snapshotEmission`) fires
  after each structural reconcile — after the routing maps reflect the new subtree
  — so the host reconciles origin connections against the live `proxyViews` map
  (a proxy lives exactly while its node is in the retained tree, spec/PROXY.md §7).
- **`SizeThatFits` fit slot** (`SizeThatFits.make(Fit...)` + `Fit.of(view, minWidth)`):
  a structural slot (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17) emitting `FIT_QUERY` (LIST, ascending
  thresholds) + the single selected child — unselected candidates never transmit.
  The host routes `FIT_CHANGED` into the slot's fit sink
  (`RenderResult.fitInputs`, via `InputDispatcher`), which swaps the child through
  the structural reconcile (an unchanged index re-emits zero opcodes). The LIST
  value type is written by `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`
  (`[count][f32 × count]` arena entries). A slot's selection is **retained node
  state** (`PathlandNode.fitSelection`): a parent-subtree re-render (an outer
  slot's candidate swap, a custom style body re-run) may rebuild a nested slot
  with a default index, so the reconcile **carries the previous selection across
  the match** (`Emitter.restoreFitSelection`) — a nested fit (the player bar's
  controls slot under the root row) keeps its candidate instead of resetting to
  compact (a reset would strand the DOM client, which never re-reports an
  unchanged width). The **web-SSR full-snapshot emission** (issue #141) is an
  internal emitter mode (`Emitter.snapshotEmission(true)`, armed by
  `PathlandSession`): on mount/resync the slot emits EVERY candidate in `FIT_QUERY`
  order so the SSR renders all branches gated by CSS container queries (a no-JS
  correct first paint) — the authored DSL is unchanged. `PathlandNode.fitReported`
  gates the mount-time structural effect so the multi-candidate presentation is
  not collapsed before the renderer reports; the first `FIT_CHANGED` (recorded
  before the incoming index) downgrades the slot to the single selected child via
  the normal reconcile, and the web client unwraps the gated branches. The
  downgrade is a **clean N→1**: it keeps the SELECTED candidate's node as-is
  (retaining its id + subtree, zero churn) and removes the others — it never
  positionally diffs, because both candidates are frequently the same component
  and morphing the loser's node into the winner would relocate the winner into
  the SSR's loser wrapper and break the renderer's candidate-position CSS gate.
  **View reuse** (issue #159): the same `View` instance may not be the candidate
  of two `Fit`s — `SizeThatFits.make` rejects it (`IllegalStateException`), since
  it would be materialized once per candidate and leak shared state / ids.
  Sharing a subtree **inside** two distinct candidate roots stays allowed; every
  materialized copy gets a distinct node id. The emitter enforces the frame's
  **unique-node-id invariant** (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle) with
  `Emitter.duplicateIds` / a fail-loud guard at mount, resync, and after each
  structural reconcile, so an id-overriding pass (an identity-stable node pinning
  a playback key) can never silently corrupt an id-keyed consumer.
- **v2 authoring surface (complete)**: every concrete view exposes
  the three operations — values via the static `View.make(...)`
  (`make(Consumer<Config>)`, `make(value)` shortcuts, empty `make()`),
  `.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` (an **instance** operation — the `View` interface
  ships a `default View.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` so a bare `View` value
  (a style's `config.label()`, a `Color`, a `FitSlot`) applies modifiers too, and
  `ViewBuilder` overrides it covariantly), and (content-bearing views) `.children(View...)`
  (static first-call retained as a value-less convenience). Values are configured
  via `make(c -> …)`, the chain lives on the returned generic
  `ViewBuilder<V, C>` (`View.Config`, `Configurable<C>`, `ChildrenView`; `View`
  keeps only `body()`/`render()`/`modifiers(...)` — Java's static-vs-instance rule
----
- **Structural reactivity** (spec DSL.md §3.4): `Conditional.when(Signal<Boolean>,
  then, else)` and `when(Signal<T>, Case.of(...)...) / Case.otherwise(...)` —
  statically importable lowercase factories on a final class (mirrors
  `Signals`; `if`/`switch`/`case`/`else` are Java keywords). A structural
  container materializes as a `Group` slot (bare `VSTACK` node); the emitter's
  structural effect reconciles the slot's single child on selector change —
  position+type-stable ids, `TREE` deltas only, identical recompute emits
  **zero** opcodes, nested containers work, and the slot's subtree owns its own
  bindings. `RenderResult` routing maps are now live unmodifiable views (a swap
  updates tap/text/value/date routing after mount).
- **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.router`, spec DSL.md §4.5): `Route` (absolute
  path, `pathOnly()` strips query/fragment), `RouteTable` (literal + `:param`
  patterns, guards → `replace()` redirect, `fallback` 404), `Router`
  (`Signal<Route>` + back-stack; `navigate`/`push`/`pop`/`replace`/`back`,
  `handlePlatformNavigation`/`handleEvent`), **`Navigation`** (the ergonomic
  facade: `Navigation.navigator(initialPath).route(...).fallback(...).build()`
  collapses table + router + seeding, `Navigation.container(router)` is the slot,
  `Navigation.isActive(router, path)` → a reactive `Signal<Boolean>` for
  active-route styling, `Navigation.ROUTER` = the `EnvironmentKey<Router>`),
  **`Params`** (typed path-param access — `get`/
  `intValue`/`longValue`/`doubleValue`/`booleanValue`/`path` — replacing the raw
  `Map` in `RouteHandler`), **a bound router** (`Navigation.navigator()...
  .build(WritableSignal<String>)` — the router binds to the host-provided
  `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal: external writes are re-routed **guard-aware**,
  its own navigation is mirrored back, the initial value is guard-processed), and
  **generic scoped environment values**
  (`EnvironmentKey`/`EnvironmentValues` + the `EnvironmentBinding` modifier value
  (`environmentBinding(e -> e.key(key).value(value))`) +
  `Environment.value(key)` — the `.environment` style, hierarchical nearest-
  wins; a `NavigationContainer` scopes `Navigation.ROUTER` to its destination
  subtree and structural slots re-apply the incoming scope on re-render via
  `PathlandNode.environmentForChildren`/`Emitter.reconcileSlot`; **reads always
  return a signal** — `Environment.value(key)` → `Signal<T>`, a value injected as
  a `Signal` comes back as the same instance (bindable for reactive updates) and a
  plain value is wrapped in a constant signal; a read made before the key is bound
  returns a **lazy signal** that captures the binding on the first `.get()` during
  render, enabling the `@Environment` **field style**
  (`private final Signal<Router> router = Environment.value(Navigation.ROUTER);`)),

Let me draft:

Bare control flow = ordinary Java flow control in body()/render() whose predicate/value comes from a signal:

1. Early-return guards:
```java
public View body() {
    if (loading.get()) return Spinner.make();
    if (error.get() != null) return ErrorView.make(error.get());
    return ContentView.make(items.get());
}
```
Today: returns at mount only; later writes don't change structure. Workaround: nested Conditional.when(loading, Spinner, Conditional.when(computed(error!=null), Error, Content)) or a computed state enum.

2. switch expressions:
```java
public View body() {
    return switch (mode.get()) {
        case HOME -> Home.make();
        case USERS -> Users.make();
        default -> NotFound.make();
    };
}
```
Today: Conditional.when(mode, Case.of(...), Case.otherwise(...)).

3. Ternary/derived values in config positions (not structure):
```java
VStack.make(v -> v.spacing(dense.get() ? 4 : 8))
Text.make(t -> t.text(signedIn.get() ? "Sign out" : "Sign in"))
Button.make(...).modifiers(frame(f -> f.width(wide.get() ? 320 : 160)))
```
First two: second is today non-reactive (raw string), first non-reactive; with #88 body re-runs and diffs re-emit spacing/text. Note: text could be a Signal binding instead. But config objects like padding/style/enum can't be bound.

4. Loops over a signal collection:
```java

```
Today: no structural list container in Java DSL (Lazy* take static children; `tracks` signals are grid tracks not items). Workaround: wrap the list subtree in a Conditional-like slot keyed by the list signal (e.g. `Conditional.when(computed(() -> true), ...)`? not clean) — practically requires a custom structural slot. So this is the strongest example where #88 adds real capability/ergonomics.

Wait — is there truly no way? You could write a custom View that sets `node.structuralContent`? structuralContent is public on PathlandNode, but only emitter calls. ```java

node.structuralContent = () -> VStack...list;
```
So it's possible but internal-ish. There's no public helper. Could add `Conditional`-style `Reactive.slot(Signal<?> trigger, Supplier<View>)`. That would be the narrow alternative.

5. Compound conditions:
```java
if (signedIn.get() && !guest.get()) ...
```
Today: computed + Conditional.

Short answer: **no, not by itself.** #88 would change *when* and *how often* the emitter recomputes, not *what it puts on the wire* — provided it reuses the existing reconcile+diff path rather than emitting a fresh tree.

**Why wire volume stays delta-only**

- The wire contract is unchanged: `TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move + `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY` deltas, never serialized trees (`AGENTS.md` Principle 2).
- The generalized path is `Emitter.reconcileSlot`/`reconcileChildren` (`Emitter.java:706`, `Emitter.java:833`): it matches old vs fresh nodes by position+type, keeps ids, and emits only differing text/properties/structure. An identical recompute emits **zero** opcodes.
- Re-rendering more of the tree costs CPU (walking and diffing), not bytes. An unchanged branch produces no ops even if the root body re-ran.
- `renderFull()` (full snapshot) is only for resync/SSR; a signal change must never route there.
- Fine-grained bindings survive: a signal only *bound* to a node still emits one `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY` and doesn't trigger a body re-render (body never read it).

**Where it could *indirectly* increase traffic**

1. **Non-deterministic / identity-valued body output.** If a re-run builds a new object that isn't `equals`-equal (custom style, padding, token, list), the diff sees a change and emits `SET_PROPERTY` even though nothing semantically changed. `propertyValuesEqual` handles `float[]` and `Objects.equals` (`Emitter.java:587`), but not arbitrary identity-based values. So body must be pure/deterministic.
2. **Component-type changes at a position.** If a body re-run returns a different root component (e.g. `VStack` → `HStack`), the diff does remove+create of that subtree, not a morph — same behavior as `Conditional` swapping branches today. A coarse tracking boundary makes this more likely.
3. **Recreated controllers / non-pinned ids.** A `MediaController` created inside `body()` gets a new identity per re-run → delete/create of the `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node (and playback restart). Already documented as "controllers must be fields" (`status.md:210`).
4. **Lists.** Diff is position+type, not keyed, so reorders/reinserts churn many property ops rather than a `MOVE`. #88 would make signal-list loops easy, so this becomes a realistic wire-cost source.

**Where it could *reduce* traffic**

If today an author works around a missing reactive read by wrapping a large subtree in a `Conditional` (or by re-emitting more than needed), precise per-view tracking can narrow the reconcile scope. But that's an authoring-pattern effect, not a protocol effect.

**Net:** bytes on the wire remain exactly the actual structural/property deltas; #88 only adds recompute scope and the risk of spurious diffs from impure bodies. If you implement it, the guardrails that keep wire size unchanged are: reconcile+diff only (never `renderFull`), deterministic body, value-equality on config objects, field-held controllers, and preserving the existing node-level bindings.
If we did #88 we could remove the current Conditinals?

The user asks: "If we did #88 we could remove the current Conditionals?"

Need to answer whether Conditional could be removed if #88 implemented. Analyze:

- Conditional.when is a public DSL API (spec DSL §3.4, Java + Rust). Removing is a breaking change.
- #88 would make bare if/switch in body reactive, which subsumes Conditional's functionality for Java composite views. But:
  1. Conditional works for any View, including inline use where you don't have a composite view class, e.g. `VStack.make().children(Conditional.when(...))`. With #88, you'd need a component whose body reads the signal. You could use a lambda-view helper or a computed supplier. Without Conditional, you'd write an anonymous View or a helper; you can't put an `if` directly in an argument list. So Conditional (or some equivalent supplier-based helper) remains useful as an inline expression.
  2. Conditional is also used by NavigationContainer? No, NavigationContainer uses structuralContent directly, not Conditional. SizeThatFits uses structuralContent. So Conditional is independent.
  3. Conditional's semantics: selector is read in a tracked structural effect; content rendered untracked; it doesn't require body re-run of enclosing components. #88 per-view tracking would require a component boundary. For inline branches, there's no component boundary, so you'd need a helper anyway. So you could not fully remove the *concept*, but you could remove the class if you provide an equivalent inline helper (e.g. `Reactive.slot` / lambda view).
  4. Rust DSL: Conditional is needed because Rust's model is build() and no fine-grained body tracking? Actually Rust rebuild+diff re-runs build() when app re-emits; Conditional's build_env reads selector at build time, so it's just sugar for if/else and could be removed if build() re-runs. But Rust apps call emit with retained tree; to react they rebuild. Conditional is used in tests. Could remove but breaking.
  5. Backward compatibility: removing Conditional breaks user code and tests, and the spec's canonical table. Could deprecate instead.
  6. #88 alone doesn't make `Conditional.when(selector, then, else)` unnecessary for cases where you want to pass a pre-built View branch inline without defining a component. You'd need something like `View.of(() -> ...)` (a lambda view). If #88 tracks reads in any render(), a lambda view could work. But that's essentially a renamed Conditional.

So answer: Technically the *behavior* would be subsumed for composite bodies, but you cannot simply delete it:
- Inline branch expressions still need a supplier-based wrapper (no component boundary, no `if` in an argument).
- Conditional is public API/spec (Java + Rust), used in tests/spec examples; removal is a breaking change, better deprecate.
- NavigationContainer/SizeThatFits don't depend on it, so no internal blocker.
- Conditional's structural slot also has properties #88 might not replicate exactly: it re-renders only the slot subtree, applies captured environment, coalesces ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH properties (that's NavigationContainer-specific), supports snapshot fit etc. Conditional itself is simple.
- Also #88's tracking boundary matters: if per-view, inline slots still needed; if root-level, any body read re-renders whole tree, and Conditional would still be more targeted.

Also, there's a semantic difference: Conditional.when returns a Group slot node (a VSTACK) always, whereas #88 body if/else returns the branch's node directly. Removing Conditional changes the tree shape (no Group wrapper) — could affect layout (Group maps to VSTACK). Actually a bare if in body also returns branch node directly today. Conditional inserts a Group wrapper. So they're not wire-identical. Removing Conditional would change layout for users relying on the wrapper (probably minimal but real).

Also, Conditional supports `Signal<T>` switch with cases and null/empty slot. #88 bare switch could do that, but inline usage again.

Recommendation: Don't remove; deprecate/mark as sugar if #88 lands, or keep for inline branches and cross-language parity. If the goal is reducing API surface, replace Conditional with a smaller `Reactive.slot(trigger, supplier)` and keep inline use. But that's a breaking change requiring spec/DSL/status updates and migration.

Now I can answer well. Key points:

Could we remove Conditional if #88 lands? Partially, but not cleanly, and probably shouldn't.

1. Behavioral subsumption for composite bodies: yes, bare if/switch in body would cover branch selection, so `Conditional.when` becomes redundant *inside a component body*.

2. But Conditional is also an *inline expression* used in argument lists:
   ```java
   VStack.children(when(show, Text..., Button...))
   ```
   There's no component boundary there; #88 tracks reads during a view's render. You can't put a Java `if` inside `.children(...)` (it's an argument). So you'd still need a supplier-based wrapper — i.e., Conditional or a rename (`Reactive.slot`/`View.of(Supplier<View>)`). You can't remove the concept, only the name/shape.

3. Wire-shape difference: Conditional materializes a Group slot (bare VSTACK) around the branch; a bare `if` in body returns the branch node directly. Removing Conditional changes the retained tree shape (extra wrapper node) and thus layout/opcode stream for existing apps. It's not a drop-in equivalence.

4. It's public spec/API across languages: spec/DSL.md §3.4/§7 canonical tables, Rust `Conditional` (`lib.rs:3197`), Java `Conditional` + `ConditionalTest` (8 tests), server proxy test, docs. Removal is a breaking change (pre-1.0 so possible) and requires spec + status + migration updates.

5. NavigationContainer/SizeThatFits don't depend on Conditional (they set `structuralContent` directly), so no internal blocker.

6. #88 tracking boundary matters: if root-level coarse tracking, Conditional is still a more targeted tool; if per-view, inline use still needs a helper.

7. Recommendation: don't remove. Either:
   - Keep Conditional as the inline/cross-language slot and let #88 cover composite bodies (two ways to do the same thing — acceptable, like SwiftUI has both `if` in ViewBuilder and explicit conditionals), or
   - If reducing API surface is the goal, replace Conditional with a smaller general `Reactive.slot(trigger, supplier)` / `View.of(Supplier<View>)` and deprecate `Conditional` over a release; keep a migration note and update spec/DSL + Rust parity.
   - Deprecate `Conditional` only after #88 lands and after `View.of(...)`-style inline helper exists.

8. Also: Conditional's switch `Case` API is convenient for enums and provides empty-slot semantics; bare switch can express it but inline again needs helper.

9. Tests: removing ConditionalTest loses coverage of structural reconcile mechanics (but those should move to #88 tests).

Since plan mode, I should present analysis and maybe a plan option. The user asks "could remove?" — answer: yes in principle for in-body branches, but not entirely; you'd still need an inline supplier helper, and removal is breaking/spec-wide. Recommend deprecate not remove.

I should also note that #88 is not currently implemented; the question is hypothetical. If they want, I can draft a plan for either "keep both" or "replace with Reactive.slot". Ask which.

One more nuance: Conditional's structural slot owns its subtree bindings and is scoped; #88 per-view would need equivalent. Also Conditional supports nested containers and fit selection restore via reconcileChildren—same machinery. So the mechanics are shared; Conditional is a thin wrapper over `PathlandNode.structuralContent`. So "removing" is really just replacing the thin API. The cost is mostly migration/spec, not engine complexity.

Actually, that's a strong point: Conditional is thin (a Group node + structuralContent supplier). If #88 lands, Conditional's implementation could be reimplemented on top of the new tracking (or remain). Removing it wouldn't simplify the engine much. So low benefit, high churn.

Answer structure:
- Short: Behaviorally yes for in-body branches; API-wise no/not worth it.
- Three reasons: inline argument use, wire/tree shape, public cross-language spec.
- What you could do instead: keep; or deprecate in favor of a generic inline helper after #88.
- Note internals: Conditional is a thin wrapper; NavigationContainer/SizeThatFits don't use it; tests/spec reference it.

I'll write.

Behaviorally, **mostly yes** — but API-wise, no, and it isn't worth it.

**What #88 would subsume**

For a composite view's `body()`, a plain `if`/`switch` reading a signal covers everything `Conditional.when` does today. `Conditional` itself is thin: a `Group`/`VSTACK` node with `node.structuralContent = supplier` (`Conditional.java:100`). Navigation and fit don't use it — `NavigationContainer` and `SizeThatFits` set `structuralContent` directly — so there's no internal dependency to untangle.

**Why you can't just delete it**

1. **Inline use.** `Conditional` works as an expression in an argument list:
   ```java
   VStack.children(when(show, Text.make(...), Button.make(...)))
   ```
   There's no component boundary there for #88 to track, and Java has no `if` expression for statements like this. You'd still need a supplier-based wrapper — i.e. `Conditional` renamed to `Reactive.slot`/`View.of(Supplier<View>)`. The concept survives; only the name changes.
2. **Tree shape.** `Conditional` always materializes a Group slot (bare `VSTACK`); a bare `if` in `body()` returns the branch node directly. Removing it changes the retained tree and emitted opcodes for existing apps — not a drop-in swap.
3. **It's public, cross-language contract.** `spec/DSL.md` §3.4/§7 canonical tables, Rust `Conditional` (`lib.rs:3197`), Java `ConditionalTest` (8 tests), `ProxyIntegrationTest`, and renderer docs (`TRANSITION` for "a `Conditional.when` branch change") all reference it. Removal is a breaking spec + status + migration change.

**Also boundary-dependent**

If #88 is implemented at root level (coarse re-render), `Conditional` remains the more targeted tool. If per-view, inline branches still need a helper.

**Recommendation**

Don't remove it. Either keep both (composite bodies get bare control flow; `Conditional` stays for inline/cross-language use — SwiftUI has the same duality), or, if reducing surface is the goal, introduce a generic `Reactive.slot(trigger, supplier)` / `View.of(Supplier<View>)`, reimplement `Conditional` on top of it, and deprecate `Conditional` over a release with a spec/status/migration update. Deleting it outright saves almost no engine complexity and costs a breaking change across Java + Rust + spec.

Key technical question: How to implement reactive body reads with minimal architecture change?

Current flow: `Emitter.mount(root, env)` calls `root.render(env)` once, gets PathlandNode tree. Composite `View.render` default calls `body()` then resolved.render(env). So to track per-view, the natural insertion point is `View.render` default (for composite views). But primitives override render and might read signals too (e.g. `Button.render` reads environment style signal, `Label` reads style, etc.). The issue says "view that reads a signal inside render()/body()". So primitives too. But primitives build a single node; tracking them means re-rendering that node and reconciling in place.

Options for implementation:

Option 1: Root-level tracked render (simplest).
- At mount, render once (untracked or tracked?), then register a root effect that re-renders the whole `root` view and reconciles the resulting tree against `this.tree`.
- But reconciling the root node itself is awkward because `this.tree` is the root; if the root component type changes, need to replace root (remove old root? The protocol root id?). Let's see how root is emitted: emitNode(tree) creates node with id. There's no explicit "root" opcode; create node 1 + insert? Let me check emitNode. If root changes type, we'd need delete old root + create new root; renderer root handling? Probably okay but may break assumptions. Alternatively wrap root in a synthetic Group at mount: root node id 1 = Group, child = actual root. Then reconcile children of the synthetic root. But this adds a wrapper node to every app (wire change, layout change) — significant. Could instead keep root node and implement `reconcileRoot` that handles same-component (common) and fallback for type change. If root type changes, we could create a new root with new id and emit delete/create; renderers might not support root replacement. Need to check renderers. Could be messy.

- Tracking: run `root.render(env)` inside `Signals.effect(() -> ...)` at mount. But the effect must register after the initial render (to avoid double). And re-render inside effect must be untracked for nested structural slots to avoid double subscription (or intentionally track all reads). If root effect tracks ALL reads including node-level text signals? Text signals aren't read in render (they're stored). Structural slot selectors are read in render; we'd want to exclude them (their own effects) or let root re-render handle them too. If root effect subscribes to slot selectors, then slot change triggers root re-render AND slot effect; duplicate but diff suppresses. However root re-render recreates slot views, destroying/re-registering effects, potentially causing effect churn. Could work but messy.

- On root re-render, we need to destroy old bindings, re-register, re-collect inputs, etc. Similar to reconcileSlot. This is substantial but doable.

Option 2: Per-view tracked render (matches issue's "any node whose render depends").
- Modify `View.render` default to wrap body evaluation in a tracked slot. But composite body returns a View, then `resolved.render(env)` is called. The emitter needs to know the resulting node and its parent position to reconcile later.
- Could assign a "render slot" object per composite view invocation, with a stable slot id and a parent slot. At mount, build a slot tree parallel to the node tree. Each slot owns a supplier that re-renders its body and produces a fresh node subtree. On dependency change, re-render that slot's subtree and reconcile against its retained node, requiring the parent to know its position. This is essentially a component-level retained tree (like React). Significant refactor: Emitter currently assumes a static node tree; structural slots are the only dynamic units.
- Inline structural slots (Conditional) are just explicit slots; generalizing means making every composite view a slot. That's a big architectural change but arguably cleaner long-term (component-level reactivity).
- But it adds per-component bookkeeping and possibly wrapper semantics? No wrapper node needed if the slot maps directly to the body's node and the parent slot tracks children. But node ids and parent-child relationships need slot-aware reconciliation. Complex.

Option 3: Opt-in tracked render via a new wrapper view (e.g. `Reactive.body(Supplier<View>)` or `View.of`), not automatic. This is basically a generalized Conditional/structural slot that can return arbitrary content and track any signal reads. It would let you write:
```java
View.of(() -> signedIn.get() ? Home.make() : Login.make())
```
and remove Conditional, since `View.of` covers if/switch inline and in body. It does NOT require body re-run or per-view tracking; it's an explicit tracked slot. But then #88's "any signal read in body" isn't automatic; authors still wrap. However, if the goal is to remove Conditional and keep one mechanism, `View.of` is a cleaner, smaller step. It also naturally covers loops:
```java
View.of(() -> VStack.make().children(tracks.get().stream().map(TrackRow::make)...))
```
This might be the best plan: implement a general "reactive subtree" (`View.of(Supplier<View>)` or `Reactive.slot`) built on `structuralContent`, use it to replace Conditional, and optionally later make composite bodies auto-tracked. But the user specifically asked about #88 and removing Conditional. They may want the full thing.

Option 4: Root-level tracking only for views that opt in via a marker interface (e.g. `ReactiveView`), so authors declare body is reactive. This avoids re-running everything.

Given plan mode, I think the right move is to ask the user which architecture they want, presenting tradeoffs, before writing the final plan. The key decision is tracking boundary. Also whether to remove Conditional or replace with a generic slot, and Rust scope.

Snapshot mode remains true for the session lifetime (set true and never false). It only affects the mount render via ThreadLocal; live reconciles render single child. The root effect's initial run would render with `SNAPSHOT_EMISSION` false (ThreadLocal reset after mount), so fit slots would produce single selected child, and diff against the snapshot tree (all candidates) → collapse. That would break the SSR first paint before the client reports FIT_CHANGED. Need to gate the root effect: skip its initial run (and any runs) until the first FIT_CHANGED? But if the root effect never runs, body reads aren't tracked. We could:
- Register the root effect only after the first `FIT_CHANGED` (or after `fitReported` on all slots). But signals read in body before that won't be tracked; any change before the first fit report would be lost. Acceptable? Maybe.
- Or make the root effect's first run preserve snapshot by setting `SNAPSHOT_EMISSION` true for that run, so it renders all candidates again and diff zero. Subsequent runs live. But then any body read is tracked during the snapshot run too, so dependencies recorded. Good. Implement: in `reconcileRoot`, if it's the first run and `snapshotEmission` is true, set ThreadLocal true during render. But the mount tree may already have been downgraded by a FIT_CHANGED before the effect's first run? The effect runs immediately at mount (before any FIT_CHANGED), so it's snapshot. Good. If a fit change occurs later, root effect re-renders live (single candidate) and the slot's own effect also reconciles. Fine. But wait: the root effect's first run with snapshot=true re-renders all candidates; the fresh tree is identical to the mount tree; zero ops. Good. Then on first FIT_CHANGED, the slot effect reconciles N→1; root effect also subscribes to fit index (because SizeThatFits.render reads `fitIndex.get()` for `node.fitSelection` — that read is during render and would be tracked!). So root effect would also fire on FIT_CHANGED and re-render whole tree live. That's okay but coarse. Or untrack `fitIndex.get()` in SizeThatFits.render (it's a selection read; the slot's own effect tracks it via supplier). Should untrack to avoid root re-render on fit changes. Similarly NavigationContainer reads router.destination() during render (initial child) and would be tracked. Could untrack. But then root effect won't fire on route changes—NavigationContainer's own effect handles it. Good. So the rule: explicit structural slots' selector reads are untracked from the root body. Implement by wrapping in `Signals.untracked` in those slots' render methods. This also means the root effect doesn't subscribe to fit/router signals, reducing coarse re-renders. But if a bare body reads the same signal, it's tracked (because it's outside the slot). Good.

However, `SizeThatFits.render` reads `fitIndex.get()` for `node.fitSelection` and then `selectedView()` in the live branch. Both should be untracked from root. But `structuralContent` supplier reads fitIndex during reconcileSlot's tracked effect (not untracked). So wrap only the initial render reads in `Signals.untracked`. Similarly `NavigationContainer.render` reads `router.destination()`; wrap in untracked. `ConditionalWhen.render` reads `content.get()`; if we remove Conditional, no need; if keep, wrap.

But there's a catch: `Signals.untracked` clears the entire stack, so it also prevents nested effects? It just clears ReactiveContext stack; any effect created inside untracked runs with its own context when scheduled. Fine. But `untracked` around `candidate.render(env)` would also prevent tracking of any signals read in the candidate's body by the root effect. That's desired? If the candidate is rendered as part of a structural slot, its body reads should perhaps be tracked by the root effect? Hmm. With root-level tracking, we want *all* body reads (including inside structural slot candidates) to be tracked so bare control flow inside them works. If we wrap the entire `selected.render(env)` in untracked, then body reads inside the candidate won't be tracked. That's bad. We only want to untrack the *selector* read, not the content render. But the initial child render is part of building the subtree; if we render content tracked, root effect subscribes to content's body reads (good). The selector read should be untracked. So:
```java
View selected = Signals.untracked(() -> content.get());
PathlandNode child = selected == null ? null : selected.render(env); // tracked
```
But `selected` may be a view instance built by the supplier; rendering it tracked is fine. In `reconcileSlot`, content render is untracked because the slot effect should not subscribe to content reads (they're owned by the child's bindings / root effect?). Wait, with root-level tracking, if the slot's own effect renders content untracked, body reads inside content won't be tracked by the root effect either (because the reconcile happens inside the slot effect, not the root effect). So bare control flow inside a route destination wouldn't re-render on signal changes! This is a key issue.

In root-level tracking, the root effect is the only body tracker. But structural slots re-render their content inside their own effects, untracked. So content body reads after a slot reconcile aren't tracked. At mount, root effect's first run renders the whole tree (including slot content) tracked, so dependencies are recorded at mount. But when the slot re-renders content, the root effect's dependencies remain from the previous render (which included the old content's reads). If the new content reads different signals, the root effect won't know. On the next root re-render, it would update dependencies. But a signal read only by the new content won't trigger the root effect until some other dependency changes. So bare control flow inside a slot-reconciled destination can be stale. This is a real limitation of root-level tracking combined with slot-owned reconciliation.

Options:
- In slot reconcile, render content tracked by the slot effect (not untracked), so the slot effect subscribes to body reads in its subtree. Then a body read change re-renders the slot subtree. That's per-slot tracking, which is exactly what we want! The current `reconcileSlot` uses `Signals.untracked` for content to keep fine-grained node bindings; but if we want body reads to re-render, the slot effect should track them. However, then any signal read in content body (including `Environment.value` style reads) subscribes the slot effect, causing subtree re-renders. That's the desired #88 behavior at slot granularity. But node-level text/property signals aren't read during render, so they don't subscribe. So changing `reconcileSlot` to render content *tracked* (not untracked) would make structural slots reactive to body reads within their content. Combined with root-level tracking, body reads anywhere are tracked: root-level for top-level, slot-level for slot content. But then the root effect also tracks reads inside slot content during its full re-render, causing double subscription (root + slot). We could untrack slot content in the root render? But root doesn't know. Hmm.

Maybe the cleanest model is: **every render call tracks its own reads**, not a single root. That's per-view tracking again. Or: **structural slots track their content reads; the root tracks everything outside slots; during root re-render, slot content is untracked (because the slot effect owns it)**. This requires the slot to signal to the root render "don't track inside me". Could use a mechanism: when rendering a structural slot, push a "barrier" so reads inside are tracked by the slot effect, not root. But the root effect's render calls `slot.render(env)`, which builds initial children; if we want the slot effect to own content tracking, the slot render should not render content at all under root; instead the slot's effect (registered after) renders content. But at mount, we need initial children for emission. We could render initial content untracked (as now), and then the slot effect's first run re-renders content tracked. Since the slot effect is registered after mount and runs immediately, it would re-render content tracked and diff zero. That's the current behavior with `untracked`; change it to tracked so the slot effect subscribes to body reads. Then:
  - Root effect (if any) tracks reads outside slots. During root re-render, slot render's initial content is rendered untracked (as now), so root doesn't subscribe to content reads. Slot effect owns them.
  - This gives hierarchical tracking: root body + each slot subtree. Nested slots own their content. Exactly the issue's "render a subtree as a tracked computation" generalized.
  - But what about bare control flow in a composite body that is *not* inside a structural slot? Root effect tracks it. Good.
  - What about a composite view inside a slot whose body reads a signal? Slot effect tracks it (since content render tracked). Good.
  - What about a composite view inside a *non-slot* parent body? Root effect tracks it (whole tree). Good.
  - So the model: root effect + slot effects each track their own subtree, with slot boundaries as tracking barriers. This is essentially "tracked subtree" at the root and at each structural slot. It's not per-component, but per-slot, which may be sufficient for most control flow (control flow is usually at the root or in route destinations).
  - However, a signal read in a deep component body inside the root (not in a slot) subscribes the root effect → whole tree re-render. Coarse but correct.
  - A signal read in a deep component inside a slot subscribes the slot effect → slot subtree re-render. Better.

This is a coherent, incremental design: **generalize reconcileSlot's tracked computation to the root and make slot content rendering tracked.** The root effect is new; slot effects already exist but currently untrack content. Changing slot content render from untracked to tracked is a behavior change: the slot effect will now subscribe to any signal read during content render. That's #88 at slot granularity. But it may also subscribe to environment/state signals read by primitives during render (e.g. `Button.render` reads `Environment.value(BUTTON_STYLE).get()`). If BUTTON_STYLE changes, slot re-renders; fine (rare). More concerning: `applyController` reads media signals — but that's done in `materializeControllers` during reconcile, which is inside the slot effect; currently `materializeControllers` is called in reconcileSlot and reads controller signals via `.get()`. If the slot effect is tracking, it would subscribe to media playback signals, causing slot re-render on every time update! Must wrap `materializeControllers` in untracked (already maybe). In `reconcileSlot`, `materializeControllers(fresh)` is called inside the effect. Need `Signals.untracked(() -> materializeControllers(fresh))`. Also `collectInputs` no signal reads. `guardUniqueIds` no. `restoreFitSelection` untracked. `registerBindings` creates effects; no reads in the slot effect itself (effects are separate). Good.
  - `renderStructuralContent` for restoreFitSelection is untracked.
  - `reconcileChildren`/`reconcileNode` use `currentText` which untracks text bindings. `propertyValuesEqual` no reads. Good.
  - `SizeThatFits.render` reads `fitIndex.get()` and `selectedView()`; if called during a tracked slot effect (nested slot), it would subscribe the outer slot to the inner fit signal. Could cause outer re-render on inner fit change; maybe okay but coarse. Could untrack selector reads in slot render as discussed. But then inner slot effect owns it. Fine.
  - `NavigationContainer.render` reads router.destination(); untrack to avoid parent subscribing.
  - `ConditionalWhen.render` reads content.get(); untrack if kept.
  - `View.render` default calls `state.connect(this)`, which may create persist effects; no direct reads in the current context? `PersistentState.signal` if existing returns; if new, creates `Signals.effect` (separate context) and reads store. No signal reads in current context. Good.
  - Primitive views reading `Environment.value(...).get()` for styles: if the environment value is a signal (e.g. `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH`), the slot/root effect subscribes. That might be desired or not. For `ButtonStyle`, usually constant. For `Navigation.isActive` it's a computed used as a binding, not read in render. Fine.

So the design can be: root tracked effect + slot effects track their content. This is a moderate change, not a full per-view refactor. It matches the issue's suggested "generalize reconcileSlot: render a subtree as a tracked computation" — the root becomes a slot, and slot content is tracked.

But wait: the issue says "any node whose render depends on a signal should emit its structural changes when that signal changes." With root + slots, a component inside a non-slot subtree re-renders the whole root, not just itself. It still emits only structural changes (diff), so observable wire is correct; CPU coarse. The issue's non-negotiable "Preserve fine-grained per-node reactivity elsewhere — an unchanged node still emits zero opcodes" is satisfied. So root + slot granularity meets the contract, with coarser recompute. Good.

Now, removing Conditional: If root tracking + slot tracking works, bare `if`/`switch` in body works. `Conditional` can be removed or kept. For inline branches, you need a helper. Could replace with `View.of(Supplier<View>)` implemented as a structural slot (Group node + structuralContent). Since slot effects now track content, `View.of` also makes content body reads reactive. and switch inside the supplier. For loops:

Let me craft concise options with recommendations.

Q1: Tracking granularity.
- "Root + structural slots (Recommended)": one root tracked computation plus each existing slot tracks its content; bare if/switch/loops work everywhere; coarse re-render for non-slot subtrees; wire stays delta-only; moderate change.
- "Per-view/component tracking": each view's render is its own tracked slot; finest CPU scope; large emitter refactor (emitter-driven render, parent/index bookkeeping, flattened-composite rules).
- "Keep explicit slots only": no automatic body tracking; add a generic View.of slot; smallest change; no bare control flow.

Q2: Conditional.
- "Replace with View.of(Supplier<View>) (Recommended)": remove Conditional/Case (Java), migrate tests/spec; View.of is the inline/supplier form, bare control flow in bodies.
- "Keep Conditional alongside": least churn; two ways.
- "Remove with no inline helper": authors define tiny views for inline branches; most churn.

Q3: Rust scope.
- "Java-only (Recommended)": #88 in the Java emitter; leave Rust's build-time Conditional or remove it separately.
- "Remove Rust Conditional too": align DSL (Rust uses plain if/match in build); update Rust test/spec.

# Plan: Reactive body (#88) + replace `Conditional` with `View.of`

## Locked decisions

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Tracking granularity | **Root + structural slots** — one tracked root computation; each existing slot tracks its content |
| Conditional | **Replace** with `View.of(Supplier<View>)` (Java), delete `Conditional`/`Case` |
| Languages | **Java gets #88**; **Rust `Conditional` is removed** too (Rust keeps its rebuild+diff model, no engine tracking) |
| Root changes | **Require a stable root component**; throw a clear error otherwise |

## Contract after this change

- `body()` / `render()` is re-evaluated when **any signal read during it** changes. The subtree is re-rendered and diffed; only actual `TREE`/`PARAMETER` deltas go on the wire.
- Tracking boundaries are the **root** and each **explicit structural slot** (`NavigationContainer`, `SizeThatFits`, `View.of`). Content inside a slot is owned by that slot's effect; the enclosing computation does not subscribe through it.
- **Non-signal reads remain mount-time only** (plain fields, mutable POJOs) — this is unchanged and documented.
- An unchanged recompute emits **zero opcodes**; no protocol/wire-format change (version stays 1).
- Root component type must stay stable across re-renders. Wrap a conditional root in `View.of`/a stable container.
- `View.of` keeps a Group-backed slot node (as `Conditional` did); bare `if` in `body()` returns the branch node directly, so the two differ in tree shape.

## Implementation

### 1. Emitter: root tracked computation (`Emitter.java`)

- Refactor `mount` so the **initial render runs inside the root effect** rather than rendering first and re-rendering:
  - Store `rootView` + `env`; create the root effect; its first run performs the current mount render/emit (ids, controllers, inputs, `emitTheme`/`emitNode`, `registerBindings`) and produces the `RenderResult`; later runs call `reconcileRoot()`.

  - Add the root effect to `bindings` so `destroy()` stops it.
- Add `reconcileRoot()` reusing the slot reconcile lifecycle:
  - Render `rootView` (snapshot mode only on the first run when `snapshotEmission` is set).
  - `materializeControllers(fresh)` and `restoreFitSelection` inside `Signals.untracked` (media reads must not subscribe the root).
  - Enforce `fresh.component == tree.component`; otherwise throw with guidance to wrap in a stable container.
  - Preserve the root id, `destroySubtreeBindings(tree)`, `forgetInputs(tree)`, `reconcileNode(tree, fresh, ops)`, emit one frame only if `ops` is non-empty, set `tree = fresh`, `collectInputs`, `registerBindings`, `guardUniqueIds`, `fireStructureReconciled`.
  - Reset `navigateHandler` before re-collecting; keep `nextId` monotonic and `mediaControllerIds` pinned.
  - Never call `renderFull()` on a signal change.
- Snapshot/#141: keep rendering candidates in snapshot mode until the first `FIT_CHANGED`. Clear `snapshotEmission` on the first fit input (wrap `fitInput` in `collectInputs`) so later root re-renders are live.
- No changes to `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink` or the transport.

### 2. Slot content tracking (`Emitter.reconcileSlot`)

The user asks: "Explain when 'Coarse CPU:' is relevant" — they want clarification on the coarse CPU risk in the plan. I need to explain concretely when root-level tracking causes whole-tree re-renders vs when slot boundaries limit it, and what the actual cost is (render + diff CPU, allocations), and when it matters in practice.

I should be concrete:
- Root-level tracking: any signal read during render outside a structural slot subscribes the root effect. When it changes, `reconcileRoot` re-runs the entire `root.render(env)` — reconstructs the whole PathlandNode tree (new objects, ids matched later), walks it to diff, re-registers bindings, re-collects inputs. That's O(tree size) CPU + allocations per change, even if only one small branch changed.
- Slot-level: reads inside a slot's content are owned by that slot effect (because we render slot content tracked and use tracking barriers). Change re-renders only that slot's subtree, O(slot subtree size).
- So coarse CPU is relevant when:
  1. A signal is read in a component body that is NOT inside a structural slot (e.g. root-level layout, a deeply nested component under the root, a plain subtree).
  2. The signal changes frequently (typing, slider drag, media position, scroll, animation ticks, viewport resize). E.g. a body reads `position.get()` to compute a label or control flow at root → every media time update re-renders whole tree at ~30Hz. Bad.
  3. The tree is large (music player, kitchensink, real apps with hundreds/thousands of nodes).
  4. Many such reads at different depths; each subscribes root, so any one change re-renders everything.
  5. Combined with derived config (spacing, colors) that body computes from frequently-changing signals.
- When it's NOT relevant:
  1. Reads are rare/one-shot signals (auth state, theme mode, route mode) that change on user action, not per frame.
  2. Reads are inside NavigationContainer destinations or SizeThatFits/View.of slots → slot-scoped.
  3. Signal is bound to a node (text/property) rather than read in body → node-level fine-grained effect, no re-render at all. This is the recommended path for frequently changing values.
  4. Small trees / SSR-only where deltas are batched and CPU is not hot.
- Note the wire is unaffected: only deltas. So it's purely server/emitter CPU (and GC/alloc) per session, which matters for SSR/WebSocket server throughput with many sessions, and for desktop single app it's usually fine.

**When coarse CPU is relevant**

Alternative: per-component tracking without changing all child render calls, using a post-mount "owner" pass with a second render. But that doubles mount work and body side effects. Not great.

Another alternative: **track per-view using a thread-local current slot, set by a wrapper around `View.render`**. The wrapper can be applied centrally if we rename the interface method and make `render` final? For example:
- Rename the primitive method to `renderNode(Environment)` (protected/abstract) and make `render` a final default method that calls `env.emitter().renderView(this, env)`.
- Composite views use `body()`; primitives override `renderNode`.
- `renderView` sets up the slot/effect and calls `view.renderNode(env)` (or `body()` for composites).
- Children: primitives call `child.render(env)`, which is the final wrapper → automatically creates child slots. **No changes to child call sites!** This is the key.

- For composite views, the default `body()` + default `renderNode` behavior: `renderNode` for a composite evaluates `body()` and renders the resolved view. But if it calls `resolved.render(env)` (the wrapper), that creates a child slot; the outer slot has no node of its own. We can make the outer slot a "transparent" slot that delegates to the child slot, or set the outer slot's node = child's node and avoid double ownership. Simpler: for composites, `renderView` evaluates `body()` tracked and then calls `resolved.render(env)` (wrapper) to get the node; the outer slot's effect tracks reads in `body()` and, on re-render, re-evaluates body and reconciles the returned child slot's node. But the child slot is nested under the outer slot? The child slot was created during the outer slot's effect run; its parent context is the outer slot's parent node. This creates a slot tree where the outer slot and inner slot both target the same parent/index. Need care.
- Alternatively, treat composite views as transparent: don't create a slot for a composite whose `body()` returns another view; just evaluate `body()` inside the **caller's** slot. But then reads in the composite body subscribe the caller's slot, which might be the root or parent component. That's still per-component-ish: the caller is the component that rendered this composite. Hmm.
- Better: make every `render` call (including composites) a slot. The slot owns the node returned by its render. For a composite, its `render` returns the node from `body().render(env)`. The inner view's render also creates a slot. Both slots own the same node. To avoid double ownership, define that a slot owns the node only if it directly created it (primitive), and composite slots are "body slots" that own their child slot, not the node. On re-render, the body slot re-evaluates body; if the resolved view identity/type changes, it replaces the child slot and reconciles the node. If the resolved view is the same instance, it can delegate re-render to the child slot. This is React's element/component tree.
- This is implementable but intricate. For a POC, maybe simpler: **component boundary = every composite view**, and when a composite body returns another view, the outer composite's slot owns the whole subtree (re-renders it). That's still a per-component boundary (the outermost composite), but nested composites' reads subscribe the outer composite, not themselves. In practice, control flow is often at a screen/component boundary; this is acceptable and much simpler. The rule: "a signal read in a composite's body (including nested composite bodies it returns) re-renders that composite's subtree." Hmm, but then a nested component's read re-renders the outer component, which may be coarse. Yet the outer component is a natural boundary; developers can split components to narrow. This is similar to React if nested components are inlined via method calls rather than elements. It's still far better than root.
- To make nested composites their own boundaries, we'd need the slot tree. But maybe we can do it: when a composite's `render` is called, create a slot; evaluate body; render resolved via `resolved.render(env)` which creates a child slot; return the child's node. The outer slot's retained node is the child's node (alias). On re-render, the outer slot re-evaluates body and calls `resolved.render(env)` again; the child slot is recreated? The emitter can reconcile the new child node against the old node in place. The outer slot's effect tracks body reads; the child slot's effect tracks its own render reads. Both effects target the same node. If a body read changes, outer re-renders and re-renders child; if a child read changes, child re-renders in place. The outer effect also tracks child reads if it renders the child inside its effect (unless untracked barrier). We can make the outer effect render the child untracked, so child reads belong to the child slot. Then each composite is its own boundary. Node aliasing: outer slot doesn't own the node; it owns the child slot. On re-render, outer re-evaluates body; if the resolved view is a new instance but same type, the child slot re-renders; if different type, reconcile/replace. This is feasible.
- The final wrapper method `render` is called by the parent's render (which runs inside the parent's slot effect). The child's `render` creates a child slot and runs its first render inside the parent's effect? To track the child's reads separately, `render` must run the child's render inside the child's own effect, not the parent's. But effects run synchronously and can be created during a parent effect. So `render` can create the child slot effect; its first run renders the child. The parent effect calls `render` and gets the node; the child effect is registered and will run (immediately? If created inside the parent effect, Scheduler queues it until the parent effect finishes). But the parent needs the node synchronously to attach it. We could render the child untracked in the parent, create the child effect with `manualCleanup` and run it manually after, but then it re-renders. Or create the child effect and run it synchronously (not via Scheduler) while suppressing parent tracking: push the child effect's context, render, pop. That's possible if `Effect` exposes a synchronous run. `Effect` is package-private; the emitter is in a different package (`dev.pathland.view.emit`), so it can't access. Could add a public/internal API in `signals` to run a tracked computation synchronously and return a value. That's a small addition: `Signals.tracked(Supplier<T>)` that pushes a temporary ReactiveNode? Or an `Effect` with a result. This is the core primitive needed for per-view tracking.
  - Implement `Signals.tracked(Supplier<T> fn)` that creates a reactive node, runs fn synchronously with tracking, and returns the value plus a handle to re-run. Could be built on `Effect` internals.

But nested `render` calls inside would also use `tracked`, and the outer `tracked` would track the inner's reads unless the inner's tracked computation clears the parent context. `Signals.untracked` clears the whole stack; `tracked` could push its own node, so inner reads register on the inner node, not the outer. That's exactly what we want: each render call is its own tracked computation, and nested renders don't leak dependencies to the parent. So `tracked` naturally provides per-view boundaries without barriers!

  - The emitter's `reconcile` callback for a slot re-renders that slot and reconciles its node in place (parent/index known).

    - A `Signals.tracked(Supplier<T>)` API with re-run callback and handle.

We can have the child slot store its node, and the parent node's children list is built by the parent render. On re-render of the outer slot, it re-renders and may produce a new node; the parent/index is known. On re-render of the inner slot, same. Both may reconcile the same node; if both are dirty, order matters. Could mark the outer slot as "transparent" and not create a separate slot for composites that return a view? Then only the innermost slot owns the node; outer body reads subscribe the parent slot (caller). Hmm.

Let me draft the response.

You're right. Root + slots makes performance depend on two things a developer can't see:

1. **Where the read sits** — inside a slot or not. `if (player.position().get() > 30)` in a screen body looks identical whether it re-renders the screen or the whole app.
2. **Whether the value is read or bound** — `Text.make(t -> t.text(time))` is free; `if (time.get() > 30)` is a subscription.

That's a hidden model, and “read the docs” is not a good answer for a POC that wants SwiftUI-like ergonomics. The slot boundaries are an implementation detail leaking into app performance.

There are only three honest ways out:

No slot-placement knowledge; high-frequency state is isolated by extracting a component (or binding it). This is the React/SwiftUI model. Cost: real refactor — a final `render` wrapper that runs each view’s render as a tracked computation, plus parent/index linking and a slot tree (~50 `render` overrides renamed, emitter changes, larger test surface). But it removes the cliff rather than documenting it.

I’d drop C as the primary design. If bare control flow is the goal, A is the consistent choice; if minimal risk is the goal, B is the consistent choice.

The user asks: If we take A (per-component tracking) and a view has 3 text children and one of them changes, how much is emitted over the wire? All 3 texts or just the changed one? If only one, how is it ensured?

I need to explain the mechanism in detail, grounded in the code. Key: per-component tracking + diff. The component re-renders its body (creating 3 fresh Text nodes), then the emitter reconciles against the retained tree, comparing each node's text/properties by id and value. Only the changed text emits SET_TEXT. The other two are equal → zero ops. This is ensured by:
- Stable ids: `reconcileChildren` matches old/fresh by position+component and assigns `fresh.id = old.id` (Emitter.java:833-...).
- Text comparison: `reconcileNode` computes `currentText(fresh)` and compares to `old.text` (last-emitted text kept current by bindings), emits `SET_TEXT` only if different (Emitter.java:870-...).

# Phase 1 Plan — Java + DSL: per-component reactive bodies (#88)

**Scope:** Java DSL + Java emitter only. Rust is untouched in Phase 1; Phase 2 is the parity plan. Breaking changes are allowed and documented.

## Target model

- **The component is the tracking unit.** Each child view expression rendered by a parent is a `ViewSlot` with its own tracked computation. A signal read in that view’s `body()`/`render()` re-renders **that slot** and diffs its subtree.
- **Root chains are flattened into one slot.** `body()` delegation, modifiers, environment wrappers, and tap/navigation wrappers stay in the same slot (`renderNode`); only child views create child slots (`render`).
- **Structural slots disappear as a special concept.** `NavigationContainer`, `SizeThatFits`, and `View.of` become ordinary components whose render reads their selector signal. `PathlandNode.structuralContent`, `structuralString/U32Property`, `environmentForChildren`, and the special `reconcileSlot` path are removed.
- **Wire is unchanged:** re-rendering is recompute; emission is still the retained-tree diff. A 3-text component whose middle text changes emits one `SET_TEXT`.
- **Root component must stay stable** (your earlier decision); nested components may change their root node type.

## Phase 1 milestones

### M0 — Render pipeline split (no behavior change)

- Rename primitive `render(Environment)` overrides to `renderNode(Environment)` across `dev.pathland.view` (~51 implementations).
- `View.render(Environment)` becomes the slot entry point: use `RenderContext.current()` if installed, else fall back to `renderNode` for direct calls/tests.
- `View.renderNode(Environment)` is the root-chain render: composites evaluate `body()` and delegate to `resolved.renderNode(env)`; wrappers delegate to `inner.renderNode(env)`; primitives build their node and call `child.render(env)` for child views.
- Add a `RenderContext` (thread-local, installed by `Emitter.mount` and by slot re-runs) holding the emitter + slot stack.
- Keep the existing structural machinery working during this milestone; run all tests to prove the rename is behavior-neutral.

### M1 — Tracked computation primitive

- Add `Signals.tracked(Supplier<T>, Consumer<T>)` (public but documented as emitter-internal):
  - Runs the supplier **synchronously** on creation and returns the value (required inside a parent render).
  - Pushes its own `ReactiveContext`, so nested tracked computations don’t leak reads to the parent.
  - Schedules a re-run on tracked dependency change and calls the consumer with the fresh value.
  - Implements `EffectRef` (`destroy()` cancels pending re-runs).
- Unit tests: synchronous first run, nested boundaries, equality suppression via `computed`, destroy/cancel, write guard.

### M2 — Slot tree + per-slot reconcile

- Add emitter-internal `ViewSlot`: owner view, captured `EnvironmentValues` scope, parent slot, child slots, retained node, node parent/index, tracked handle, slot-owned binding/input lists.
- `Emitter.renderView(view, env)`:
  - Create slot; push onto slot stack; capture `Environment.current()`; run `Signals.tracked(() -> view.renderNode(env), fresh -> reconcileSlot(slot, fresh))` with the captured scope applied and `RenderContext` installed.
  - Set `node.slot = slot` on the returned node; collect child slots created during the render.
- `Emitter.reconcileSlot(slot, fresh)`:
  - Reconcile `fresh` against `slot.node` at `slot.nodeParent`/`slot.nodeIndex` using the existing `reconcileChildren`/`reconcileNode` diff (stable ids, value equality, zero-op identical recompute).
  - If the slot has no parent node (root), reconcile in place; if the root component changes, throw the stable-root error.
  - If a nested slot’s component type changes, remove/delete the old node and create/insert the fresh node at the same index.
  - Materialize controllers (`materializeControllers`) and fit-selection restoration inside `Signals.untracked`.
  - Destroy old child slots + their tracked computations, node bindings, and routing entries; adopt fresh child slots; register fresh bindings/inputs; `guardUniqueIds`; `fireStructureReconciled` when structure/routing changed.
  - Emit one frame only when ops are non-empty.
- Add `PathlandNode` back-references (`slot`, `parent`, `index`) or an identity-map equivalent. Assign parent/index by walking the produced node tree after each slot render.
- Make node-level bindings and input routing **slot-owned**: a slot registers/destroys only its own nodes (skip subtrees owned by child slots). Preserve the global `navigateHandler` and `proxyViews` updates.
- Keep `nextId` monotonic and `mediaControllerIds` pinned across re-renders.

### M3 — Convert structural slots to components

- `NavigationContainer`: render reads `router.destination()`/`path()`/`depth()`, pushes the router scope, renders the destination as a child slot; diff emits `ROUTE`/`NAV_DEPTH` and `TREE` deltas. Remove `structuralContent`/`structuralString/U32`.
- `SizeThatFits`: render reads `fitIndex` and `SNAPSHOT_EMISSION`, renders all candidates (snapshot) or the selected candidate (live) as child slots. Keep `fitInput`, `fitReported`, and adapt `restoreFitSelection` to carry a nested fit’s selection across a parent re-render.
- `View.of(Supplier<View>)` (new): Group-backed component; render reads the supplier, renders the selected view as a child slot. This replaces `Conditional`.
- Remove `PathlandNode.structuralContent`, `structuralStringProperty`, `structuralU32Property`, `environmentForChildren`, and the old `reconcileSlot`/`renderStructuralContent` code.
- Snapshot/SSR (#141): keep a `snapshotActive` flag; the root/slot renders use `SNAPSHOT_EMISSION` while active; clear it on the first `FIT_CHANGED` so later body re-renders are live.
- Media: run controller materialization untracked on every slot render; pinned ids keep playback stable. Document that controllers must be fields.
- State: re-running a component body reconnects `State` fields (binder is idempotent); document.

### M4 — DSL surface

- Add `View.of(Supplier<View>)` as the inline control-flow/loop form.
- Delete `Conditional` + `Case` (Java) and migrate:
  - `ConditionalTest` → `ViewOfTest`.
  - `ProxyIntegrationTest` import/usage.
  - Comments in `RenderResult`, `PathlandNode`, `RouterTest`, `LabelTest`.
- Bare control flow now works in `body()`: `if`/`switch`/early returns/loops/ternaries/derived raw config.
- Update the `View` javadoc contract:
  - `body()`/`renderNode()` may run multiple times; must be pure/idempotent; no signal writes.
  - `render()` is the emitter entry point and should not be overridden.
  - Custom primitives override `renderNode`; child views use `child.render(env)`; wrappers use `inner.renderNode(env)`.
  - `Signals.untracked` is the escape hatch for deliberate non-subscribing reads.
- Migration note: `Conditional.when(sel, a, b)` → `View.of(() -> sel.get() ? a : b)`; `Case` switch → `switch` inside the supplier.

### M5 — Docs, spec, status

- `spec/DSL.md`: rewrite §3.4 (component reactive bodies; `View.of` inline; bare `if`/`switch`; loops), §6.7 reactivity discipline, §7/§8 examples.
- `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, `spec/OPCODE.md`, `spec/PROXY.md`: replace `Conditional.when` wording with “structural slot/component swap”.
- `AGENTS.md`: replace “`body()` is evaluated once at mount” with the component tracking contract; document `render`/`renderNode`, slot ownership, root stability, and non-signal semantics.
- `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`: new render model, `View.of`, removed `Conditional`, root/slot tracking, snapshot/media/State rules.
- Add a Java-first note: Rust parity is Phase 2; Rust `Conditional` remains until then.

 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear

 > **`com.pathland.view` DSL** (reusable library, Java 17+); both drive the engine
 > through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared

 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.

 arena string). Foreign hosts reach signals via the flat C ABI

 `node_bind_property`) and the Java `Signal` type. Binding then calling `emit`

   auto-loads the persisted value and auto-saves on change (key `name:scope`), and
   `StateStore` is untyped (one store serves all signal types).
 - **Fine-grained emitter** (`com.pathland.view.emit`): mounts a view tree once,
   assigns stable ids, and registers a **node-level binding effect** per reactive
   text/property — a signal change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT` /
   `SET_PROPERTY` (unchanged signals emit zero opcodes). Sinks: `FrameOpcodeSink`
   (self-contained frames for SSR/WebSocket) and `RingOpcodeSink` (JNA into
   `libpathland_core`). The wire codec (`com.pathland.view.transport`) mirrors
   `pathland_core_transport` (`PLPL` batch format, self-contained frames + events).

 tests (golden byte layout + round-trips), replacing the old codegen assert pass.
 
 - **Single signal value convention**: a view or modifier holds **one `Signal<T>`
   field** for a reactive value — never a raw field *plus* a signal field for the
   same value. Static values are authored through the raw config setter (or the
   `.of(T)` convenience), which
   wraps them in `Signals.constant(...)` (e.g. `Text.make(t -> t.text("Hello"))` ≡

   `ConstantSignal` as
   a plain, non-reactive property (no binding/effect), so statics carry zero
   binding overhead. Controls' config fields for *distinct* properties
   (`min`/`max`/`step`/`placeholder`/`mode`/`style`) stay raw.
